Capabilities

What I do, what you get, and the proof

01

AI Product Design

From model capability to a flow people trust: prompts, states, guardrails and the UI around them.

Good fit when
The model works, but the product around it doesn't feel trustworthy yet.

What you get

  • Workflow map of where the model meets the user
  • Prompt, loading, uncertainty, error and recovery states
  • Coded prototype your engineers can ship from
  • Evaluation plan: what "trust" means and how we measure it
See the work
02

Design System Build

Tokens, accessible components and spec files your engineers and AI agents can both consume.

Good fit when
Two or more surfaces, or two or more brands, keep rebuilding the same UI.

What you get

  • Primitive, semantic and component token tiers, themeable per brand
  • Core component set, WCAG 2.2 AA, in Figma and code
  • 8-section spec file per component
  • Storybook, contribution rules and a changelog
Read the Colaberry case
03

UX Audit and Redesign

A measured teardown against UX laws and WCAG 2.2, then the redesign that moves the number.

Good fit when
A live product has a conversion, engagement or accessibility number you can name.

What you get

  • Scored audit: UX laws, cognitive load, WCAG 2.2 AA
  • Prioritised fixes with expected impact
  • Redesigned flows as coded prototypes
  • Before and after measurement plan

Before you write

Full-time role or project work?

Both. Companies hiring a senior or lead product designer in KSA or UAE, on-site or remote, can start with the resume. Teams with a product problem can bring me in for a scoped project, with me doing the work.

What do you need from us to start?

Access to the product, one decision-maker, and the number you want to move. Design files and research are welcome but not required; I audit what exists in the first week.

How do you hand off?

As code and spec files, not just mock-ups: tokens, components, states and a changelog your engineers, and your AI tools, can read without me in the room.
